learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: electron source
items.prompt: A galvanic cell includes Fe(s) → Fe2+ + 2 e− and Ag+ + e− → Ag(s). Which statement identifies the electron-producing electrode?
options: Silver is the anode because Ag+ gains electrons
Iron is the anode because iron releases electrons
Silver is the cathode because silver releases electrons
Iron is the cathode because Fe2+ enters solution
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: trace electrons
items.prompt: A galvanic cell runs with Al(s) → Al3+ + 3 e− and Ni2+ + 2 e− → Ni(s). Through the external wire, electrons move in which direction?
options: From nickel to aluminum
From the salt bridge to nickel
From aluminum to nickel
From aluminum ions to nickel ions through solution
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: assign galvanic signs
items.prompt: In a galvanic cell, tin is oxidized and bromine is reduced. Which electrode-sign assignment is correct?
options: Tin anode is negative; bromine cathode is positive
Tin cathode is positive; bromine anode is negative
Tin anode is positive; bromine cathode is negative
Both electrodes are positive because the reaction is spontaneous
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: separate charge paths
items.prompt: Which description correctly separates charge transport in a working two-compartment galvanic cell?
options: Electrons cross the salt bridge while ions move through the wire
Electrons and cations both move only through the external wire
Anions carry electrons from cathode to anode through solution
Electrons use the wire; ions use the electrolyte
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: magnesium and copper
items.prompt: A galvanic cell uses Mg(s) → Mg2+ + 2 e− and Cu2+ + 2 e− → Cu(s). Which combined statement is correct?
options: Copper is the negative anode, and electrons move copper → magnesium
Magnesium is the positive cathode, and electrons move copper → magnesium
Magnesium is the negative anode, and electrons move magnesium → copper
Copper is the positive anode, and electrons move magnesium → copper
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: driven iodide cell
items.prompt: An external power source drives 2 I− → I2 + 2 e− at electrode P and Pb2+ + 2 e− → Pb at electrode Q. Which statement is correct for this electrolytic cell?
options: P is the positive anode, and the source removes electrons from P
P is the negative cathode, and the source supplies electrons to P
Q is the positive anode, and oxidation occurs at Q
Q is the negative anode, and electrons leave Q for P
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: locate oxidation
items.prompt: Which half-reaction marks an anode solely from electron placement?
options: Co3+ + e− → Co2+
2 Br− → Br2 + 2 e−
Ca2+ + 2 e− → Ca
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: cobalt and gold
items.prompt: A galvanic cell uses Co(s) → Co2+ + 2 e− and Au3+ + 3 e− → Au(s). Which statement is correct?
options: Cobalt is the negative anode, and electrons move cobalt → gold
Gold is the negative anode, and electrons move gold → cobalt
Cobalt is the positive cathode, and electrons move gold → cobalt
Gold is the positive anode, and electrons move cobalt → gold
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: preserve names, change signs
items.prompt: Which rule remains true in both galvanic and electrolytic cells?
options: The anode is always negative
Oxidation occurs at the anode
The cathode always supplies electrons to the wire
Reduction occurs at the positive electrode
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: driven sulfide cell
items.prompt: A power source drives S2− → S + 2 e− at electrode R and Sn4+ + 2 e− → Sn2+ at electrode T. Which assignment is correct?
options: R is the negative cathode; T is the positive anode
R is the negative anode; T is the positive cathode
R is the positive anode; T is the negative cathode
R is the positive cathode; T is the negative anode
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: choose reduction
items.prompt: Standard reduction potentials are Cl2 + 2 e− → 2 Cl−, +1.36 V, and Cu2+ + 2 e− → Cu, +0.34 V. In a spontaneous standard galvanic pairing, which species is reduced?
options: Cl2
Cl−
Cu
Cu2+ only after doubling +0.34 V
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: calculate E°cell
items.prompt: Ni2+/Ni has E°red = −0.25 V and Pb2+/Pb has E°red = −0.13 V. What is E°cell for the spontaneous standard galvanic direction?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: avoid coefficient scaling
items.prompt: Al3+ + 3 e− → Al has E°red = −1.66 V. Ag+ + e− → Ag has E°red = +0.80 V. After multiplying the silver half-reaction by 3 to balance electrons, which cathode potential belongs in E°cell?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: infer electron flow
items.prompt: E°red for Sn2+/Sn is −0.14 V and for Fe2+/Fe is −0.44 V. In the spontaneous standard cell, external electrons move from which electrode to which?
options: Tin → iron
Iron → tin
Tin ions → iron ions through the salt bridge
The direction cannot be inferred from reduction potentials
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: chromium and copper
items.prompt: Cr3+ + 3 e− → Cr has E°red = −0.74 V and Cu2+ + 2 e− → Cu has E°red = +0.34 V. What are E°cell and the electron-flow direction for the spontaneous standard cell?
options: +1.08 V; chromium → copper
−1.08 V; copper → chromium
+0.40 V; chromium → copper
+1.82 V; copper → chromium
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: assess reversed direction
items.prompt: A cell reaction is written so that a +0.62 V reduction is forced to run as oxidation and a −0.18 V reduction runs at the cathode. What is E°cell for the written direction, and what does its sign imply under standard conditions?
options: +0.44 V; the written direction is spontaneous
+0.80 V; coefficients must be scaled
−0.80 V; the written direction requires external driving
−0.44 V; the written direction is galvanic
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: cathode minus anode
items.prompt: Which setup correctly uses E°red(cathode) = +0.15 V and E°red(anode) = −0.52 V?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: manganese and silver
items.prompt: Mn2+/Mn has E°red = −1.18 V and Ag+/Ag has E°red = +0.80 V. What are E°cell and electron flow for the spontaneous standard cell?
options: −1.98 V; silver → manganese
+0.38 V; manganese → silver
+1.98 V; silver → manganese
+1.98 V; manganese → silver
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: interpret a negative result
items.prompt: Under the stated standard conditions, what does E°cell = −0.45 V mean for the reaction exactly as written?
options: It is nonspontaneous in that direction and needs external driving
It is spontaneous because the magnitude is positive
It becomes spontaneous when every coefficient is doubled
It has no electron transfer
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: forced reverse cell
items.prompt: A reaction direction places a −0.05 V reduction at the cathode and a +0.47 V reduction in reverse at the anode. Which conclusion is correct?
options: E°cell = +0.42 V, so the direction is galvanic
E°cell = −0.52 V, so the direction requires external input
E°cell = +0.52 V after balancing electrons
E°cell = −0.42 V, but the direction remains spontaneous
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: current to charge
items.prompt: A 2.50 A current runs for 400 s. How much charge passes?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: silver deposit
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e−. A charge of 1.93 × 10^4 C passes while Ag+ + e− → Ag. How many moles of Ag form?
options: 2.00 mol
5.00 mol
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: copper deposit
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e−. A charge of 9.65 × 10^3 C passes while Cu2+ + 2 e− → Cu. How many moles of Cu form?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: chlorine amount
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e−. During 2 Cl− → Cl2 + 2 e−, 1.93 × 10^5 C passes. How many moles of Cl2 are produced?
options: 0.50 mol
1.00 mol
2.00 mol
4.00 mol
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: aluminum mass
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e− and Al molar mass = 27.0 g/mol. A 10.0 A current runs for 2895 s while Al3+ + 3 e− → Al. What mass of Al forms?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: solve for hydrogen time
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e−. The cathode reaction is 2 H+ + 2 e− → H2. How long must a 5.00 A current run to produce 0.0500 mol H2?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: order the Faraday ladder
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly converts current and time into deposited mass?
options: I/t → moles product → coulombs → grams
It → coulombs/F → moles e− → half-reaction ratio → grams
F/It → moles product × electron coefficient → grams
It × F → moles e− → grams
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: calcium mass
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e− and Ca molar mass = 40.0 g/mol. A charge of 1.93 × 10^4 C passes while Ca2+ + 2 e− → Ca. What mass forms?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: reverse the ladder
items.prompt: To solve for time from a desired product amount, which order is correct?
options: Product moles → electron moles → coulombs → time = Q/I
Product moles → grams → current → electron moles
Time → coulombs → product moles → current
Product moles → coulombs/F → current × charge
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: oxygen time
items.prompt: Use F = 9.65 × 10^4 C/mol e−. The anode reaction produces one O2 per 4 e−. How long must an 8.00 A current run to produce 0.0200 mol O2?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: identify the driving difference
items.prompt: A cell has Zn(s)|Zn2+(0.010 M) and Zn2+(1.0 M)|Zn(s). What distinguishes the half-cells?
options: The electrode metals
The number of electrons in the zinc half-reaction
The zinc-ion concentrations
The oxidation state of solid zinc
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: place oxidation
items.prompt: In a Cu/Cu2+ concentration cell, which process on the 0.020 M side would raise its Cu2+ concentration?
options: Cu2+ + 2 e− → Cu
Cu → Cu2+ + 2 e−
Cu2+ moves through the wire
Electrons convert directly into Cu2+ in solution
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: assign electrode roles
items.prompt: Two Ni/Ni2+ half-cells contain 0.005 M and 0.80 M Ni2+. Under the stated concentration-cell model, which assignment is correct?
options: 0.005 M side is anode; 0.80 M side is cathode
0.005 M side is cathode; 0.80 M side is anode
Both sides are cathodes because the electrodes match
Neither side can transfer electrons because the metals match
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: track concentration changes
items.prompt: As an Ag/Ag+ concentration cell discharges, what happens under the stated model?
options: Both Ag+ concentrations increase equally
The dilute side becomes more dilute and the concentrated side more concentrated
Both Ag+ concentrations decrease equally
Dilute-side Ag+ rises; concentrated-side Ag+ falls
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: cobalt concentration cell
items.prompt: A Co/Co2+ cell has 0.010 M Co2+ on side L and 0.60 M on side H. Which combined statement is correct?
options: L is cathode; electrons move H → L; the gap narrows
L is anode; electrons move L → H; the gap narrows
H is anode; electrons move H → L; the gap widens
H is cathode; electrons move H → L; both concentrations rise
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: labels reversed
items.prompt: In a Sn/Sn2+ concentration cell, side A is changed from 0.020 M to 1.20 M while side B is changed from 0.90 M to 0.010 M. After this reversal, which direction should electrons move under the stated model?
options: A → B because A now has the higher concentration
No flow because both electrodes are tin
B → A because B is now the dilute-side anode
B → A because B is now the concentrated-side cathode
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: match process to concentration
items.prompt: Which pairing reduces a metal-ion concentration difference?
options: Oxidation on the concentrated side; reduction on the dilute side
Reduction on both sides
Oxidation on both sides
Oxidize dilute; reduce concentrated
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: iron concentration cell
items.prompt: An Fe/Fe2+ cell has 0.030 M Fe2+ on side X and 0.75 M on side Y. Which statement is correct?
options: X oxidizes; electrons move X → Y; the concentrations converge
Y oxidizes; electrons move Y → X; the concentrations converge
X reduces; electrons move X → Y; both concentrations fall
Y reduces; electrons move Y → X; the concentrations diverge
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: recompute from current labels
items.prompt: If the dilute and concentrated solutions are exchanged between two identical metal electrodes, what happens to their electrode roles?
options: The old anode remains anode because electrode material fixes the role
Both become cathodes
The roles reverse because the concentration condition moved
The roles become undefined until electrode metals differ
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: new reversal
items.prompt: A Pb/Pb2+ cell initially has side M dilute and side N concentrated. The solutions are replaced so M is 0.90 M and N is 0.015 M. Which assignment now applies?
options: M is anode and sends electrons to N
N is anode and sends electrons to M
M remains cathode but sends electrons to N
N is cathode because it was concentrated initially
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: series voltage
items.prompt: Four identical 1.2 V cells are connected in series. What approximate battery voltage is expected?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: lead-acid discharge
items.prompt: Which change occurs at both electrodes of a lead-acid cell during discharge?
options: Both electrodes become elemental lead
Both electrodes form PbSO4
Both electrodes release oxygen gas
Both electrodes become PbO2
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: acid concentration
items.prompt: During normal lead-acid discharge, what qualitative change is expected in the sulfuric-acid electrolyte?
options: Its concentration decreases as acid is consumed and water forms
Its concentration increases because both electrodes release sulfate
It remains exactly fixed because electrolyte never participates
It becomes an alkaline potassium-hydroxide solution
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: classify recharge
items.prompt: Which statement best describes recharging a rechargeable electrochemical cell?
options: The discharge reaction continues spontaneously in the same direction
Cell voltage is multiplied without changing chemistry
Electrons stop moving, so no redox chemistry occurs
An external source drives the net discharge chemistry in reverse
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: lead-acid stack
items.prompt: A lead-acid battery contains five approximately 2.0 V cells in series and is discharging. Which combined statement is correct?
options: About 10 V; both electrodes move toward PbSO4
About 2 V; both electrodes move toward PbO2
About 10 V; sulfuric acid concentration rises
About 4 V; both electrodes become Cd
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: nickel-cadmium charging
items.prompt: During nickel-cadmium discharge, Cd is oxidized and nickel oxyhydroxide is reduced. What must a charger drive at the cadmium electrode during recharge?
options: Further oxidation of Cd to discharge the cell faster
Reduction that restores Cd from its oxidized discharge product
Reduction of nickel oxyhydroxide at both electrodes
Conversion of the alkaline electrolyte into sulfuric acid
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: separate voltage and chemistry
items.prompt: Which reasoning sequence correctly analyzes a named multi-cell battery?
options: Use voltage to infer all products, then ignore cell count
Add chemical coefficients to cell voltage
Identify per-cell discharge chemistry, then separately combine cell voltages
Infer capacity directly from voltage and choose a redox reaction afterward
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: six-cell lead-acid battery
items.prompt: A six-cell lead-acid battery has about 2.1 V per cell and is discharging. Which statement is supported?
options: About 2.1 V total, with sulfuric acid concentration increasing
About 8.4 V total, with both electrodes becoming PbO2
About 12.6 V total, with both electrodes moving toward PbSO4
About 12.6 V total, with cadmium oxidized
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: reverse the discharge half-reaction
items.prompt: If species X is oxidized at an electrode during discharge, what process at that same electrode restores X during recharge?
options: Externally driven reduction of the oxidized product
Further spontaneous oxidation of X
No electron transfer
A voltage calculation with no chemical reversal
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: nickel-side charging fault
items.prompt: A nickel-cadmium charger restores cadmium correctly but fails to drive the nickel-electrode discharge reduction in reverse. What is the most direct consequence?
options: The cell becomes a lead-acid battery
The nickel electrode is not fully restored
Series voltage doubles without chemical restoration
Cadmium must continue oxidizing spontaneously during charging
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
